{{Short description|American physicist (1933–2018)}}
'''Donald Thorn Farley Jr.''' (October 26, 1933 – May 13, 2018) was an American [[physicist]] and Professor of Engineering at [[Cornell University]] who pioneered the use of radar [[remote sensing]] of the earth's [[ionosphere]]. He developed the theory and technique of [[incoherent scatter]] observation of the thermal fluctuations of [[plasma (physics)|plasma]]. About 80 percent of all ionospheric radio scientists in the United States who practice incoherent scatter were trained by Farley, or by his students.{{citation needed|date=November 2022}} Farley was the J. Preston Levis Professor of Engineering at [[Cornell University]]. His principal collaborators included John Dougherty, [[Tor Hagfors]], Bela Fejer, Ronald Woodman, Michael Kelley, and Wesley Swartz.<ref>{{cite news|title=Donald T. Farley Jr.|url=http://www.bangsfuneralhome.com/obituary/donald-farley-jr|accessdate=May 15, 2018|publisher=Bangs Funeral Home}}</ref>
